sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日时事通讯《交易书》（Dealbook）的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市“交易书峰会”的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、不加过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the voters in Alabama have rejected Roy Moore, giving Democrats a rare victory in the staunchly conservative state.
sentences.zh: 今天，阿拉巴马州的选民拒绝了罗伊·摩尔，让民主党在这个坚定的保守州赢得了一场难得的胜利。

sentences.en: That brings the Republican majority in the Senate down to one seat.
sentences.zh: 这使得共和党在参议院的多数席位减少到仅剩一席。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月13日，星期三。

sentences.en: I gotta tell you, I have been waiting all my life, and now I just don't know what the hell to say.
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，我一生都在等待这一刻，而现在我真不知道该说些什么好。

sentences.en: Thank you for calling the Renaissance Hotel and Spa.
sentences.zh: 感谢您致电文艺复兴酒店及水疗中心。

sentences.en: How may I assist you?
sentences.zh: 请问有什么我可以帮您的？

sentences.en: Hey, I'm trying to reach room 303.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我想找303房间。

sentences.en: Jonathan Martin.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·马丁。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Give me one moment.
sentences.zh: 请稍等。

sentences.en: Mr. Martin?
sentences.zh: 马丁先生？

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Jonathan, it's 12.02 a.m.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，现在是凌晨12点02分。

sentences.en: on Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 周三凌晨。

sentences.en: A few hours ago, Democrat
sentences.zh: 几个小时前，民主党人

sentences.en: Doug Jones was announced the winner in the Alabama special election.
sentences.zh: 道格·琼斯被宣布在阿拉巴马州特别选举中获胜。

sentences.en: When is the last time that the state of Alabama elected a Democrat to the United States Senate?
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马州上一次选举民主党人进入美国参议院是什么时候？

sentences.en: It was actually in 1992.
sentences.zh: 实际上是在1992年。

sentences.en: His name was Richard C.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫理查德·C·

sentences.en: Shelby.
sentences.zh: 谢尔比。

sentences.en: He is now the senior senator from Alabama who happens to be a Republican.
sentences.zh: 他现在是阿拉巴马州的资深参议员，碰巧是一名共和党人。

sentences.en: He changed parties and ran again in 94 as a Republican.
sentences.zh: 他在94年更换了党派并以共和党人身份再次参选。

sentences.en: But the last time that they elected a Democrat was, in fact, a quarter of a century ago.
sentences.zh: 但他们上一次选举民主党人，实际上是在四分之一个世纪前。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Jonathan, how wild is it to you for Alabama to have elected a Democrat in this moment where the political divide is so vast?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，在政治分歧如此巨大的时刻，阿拉巴马州竟然选出了一名民主党人，你觉得这有多疯狂？

sentences.en: It's striking.
sentences.zh: 这很让人震惊。

sentences.en: This is one of the most Republican states in the country, the deeply partisan state.
sentences.zh: 这是全国最坚定的共和党州之一，一个党派色彩极浓的州。

sentences.en: It's racially polarized.
sentences.zh: 这里存在明显的种族两极分化。

sentences.en: African Americans are almost entirely Democrats.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人几乎全都是民主党人。

sentences.en: And you'd have to guess about 75 percent of the population, the white population here, is Republican.
sentences.zh: 而你不得不猜想这里大约75%的人口，即白人人口，是共和党人。

sentences.en: So you've got the sort of two parties fractured along racial lines.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，两个政党大致沿着种族界限分裂。

sentences.en: What happened tonight is that you saw a swing of a lot of white voters, a good chunk of them, moderate Republicans, who just didn't want to be embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 今晚发生的事情是，你看到大量白人选民发生了动摇，其中相当一部分是温和派共和党人，他们只是不想感到尴尬。

sentences.en: They've known Roy Moore since well before the allegations from the women earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 早在今年早些时候那些女性指控他之前，他们就已经认识罗伊·摩尔很久了。

sentences.en: They have been not fond of him, shall we say, for years because they find him to be incendiary and divisive.
sentences.zh: 可以说，多年来他们一直不喜欢他，因为他们发现他具有煽动性和分裂性。

sentences.en: And I think what happened, Michael, is after these women emerged last month to accuse him of sexual misconduct, it was the last straw.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我想发生的事情是，在上个月这些女性出现指控他性骚扰之后，这成了压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: And in fact, no more was kind of a catch-all that Doug Jones, the Democrat, used to sort of implore
sentences.zh: 事实上，民主党人道格·琼斯用“拒绝更多”作为一个包罗万象的口号，用来恳求

sentences.en: moderates and even some conservatives in this state to, for a moment at least, drop their partisan preference and support a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 该州的温和派甚至一些保守派，至少暂时放下他们的党派偏好，支持民主党人。

sentences.en: Boy, you're just sitting out here in this cold.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你竟然就坐在这寒风里。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's lovely.
sentences.zh: 这感觉真好。

sentences.en: Jonathan, our colleague Jess Bidgood was down in Alabama today with you and talking to voters.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，我们的同事杰丝·比德古德今天和你一起在阿拉巴马州与选民交谈。

sentences.en: And she has this kind of fascinating exchange with a woman.
sentences.zh: 她和一位女士有一段非常奇妙的对话。

sentences.en: So, uh, so what's, what's your name?
sentences.zh: 那么，呃，你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Linda.
sentences.zh: 琳达。

sentences.en: Linda?
sentences.zh: 琳达？

sentences.en: What's your last name?
sentences.zh: 你贵姓？

sentences.en: Well, I don't want to be voted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不想被曝光。

sentences.en: Are you sure?
sentences.zh: 你确定吗？

sentences.en: But doesn't want her name used because she feels like she is alone in Alabama in being someone who won't support Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 但她不想透露自己的名字，因为她觉得自己作为不支持罗伊·摩尔的人，在阿拉巴马州是孤独的。

sentences.en: The thing is, I don't want my name in the paper because I'm probably voting differently than a lot of Alabama people are.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我不想把我的名字登在报纸上，因为我的投票选择可能和许多阿拉巴马人不同。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Oh, because you voted for, for...
sentences.zh: 哦，因为你投票给……

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: But I don't want to make my friends mad, you know?
sentences.zh: 但我不想惹我的朋友们生气，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't even know how they're voting, but, um...
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道他们是怎么投票的，但是，嗯……

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: She's a white woman and didn't want to kind of confess that to people in her world.
sentences.zh: 她是一位白人女性，不想向她生活圈子里的人坦白这一点。

sentences.en: Does that feel to you like part of the story of this election?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这像是这次选举故事的一部分吗？

sentences.en: A lot of people quietly unable to stomach Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 许多人默默地无法忍受罗伊·摩尔。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I think that's a huge part of this story is that folks not wanting to be totally honest with a pollster or with a neighbor, certainly with a reporter from out of town.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是这个故事中极其重要的一部分，那就是人们不愿意对民调人员或邻居完全诚实，当然也不愿意对外地记者诚实。

sentences.en: I may get killed, but maybe not everybody reads, but a lot of people do read the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我可能会挨骂，但也许不是每个人都阅读，但确实有很多 人阅读《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All right, so you want my last name to you?
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以你想把我的姓氏告诉我？

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 是的，拜托。

sentences.en: I'll have to spell it for you.
sentences.zh: 我得为你拼写一下。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Ten letters.
sentences.zh: 十个字母。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: B-O-H.
sentences.zh: B-O-H.

sentences.en: But who just were embarrassed by Roy Moore, and by the way, had been for years, well before these women emerged to accuse him of sexual misconduct.
sentences.zh: 但他们只是对罗伊·摩尔感到尴尬，顺便说一句，多年来一直如此，远在这些女性出现指控他性骚扰之前。

sentences.en: This is somebody who was a birther.
sentences.zh: 这是一个散布“奥巴马出生地阴谋论”的人。

sentences.en: This is somebody who said that Muslims should not be sworn in as lawmakers in this country, who even said that being gay should be illegal in this country.
sentences.zh: 这是一个声称穆斯林不应宣誓成为这个国家的立法者的人，甚至声称在这个国家同性恋应该是非法的人。

sentences.en: The other man is just not a choice for me.
sentences.zh: 另一个人对我说来根本不是选择。

sentences.en: And Doug Jones is a man of great integrity and great character.
sentences.zh: 而道格·琼斯是一个极具正直和品格的人。

sentences.en: He's a reasonable, sensible person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个讲道理、明智的人。

sentences.en: And I really agree with our other senator, Senator Shelby, that we in Alabama deserve better than Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞同我们的另一位参议员谢尔比参议员的看法，我们在阿拉巴马州值得拥有比罗伊·摩尔更好的人。

sentences.en: For that part of the electorate, it was just their moment of enough, enough.
sentences.zh: 对于那部分选民来说，这只是他们忍无可忍的时刻。

sentences.en: Let's not keep electing this person.
sentences.zh: 让我们不要再选举这样的人了。

sentences.en: Even if it's a Democrat, we can stomach him.
sentences.zh: 即使他是民主党人，我们也能接受他。

sentences.en: But we may find out that we have more people who turn Democratic with this going on, because a lot of the Republicans are saying that they just cannot vote for him.
sentences.zh: 但随着事态的发展，我们可能会发现有更多的人转向民主党，因为许多共和党人表示他们根本无法投票给他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds like you don't even want to say his name.
sentences.zh: 听起来你甚至不想说出他的名字。

sentences.en: I don't.
sentences.zh: 我确实不想。

sentences.en: It's just he doesn't deserve any kind of credit for anything.
sentences.zh: 就是他根本不配得到任何形式的肯定。

sentences.en: Crucial to Jones's victory tonight, Michael, was the fact that he won a lot of the most affluent
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，今晚琼斯获胜的关键在于，他赢得了许多该州最富裕的

sentences.en: parts of this state, you know, areas that typically support Bush or Romney style Republicans and are tax diverse, but they just couldn't stomach Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 地区，你知道的，那些通常支持布什或罗姆尼风格的共和党人、税收多样化的地区，但他们就是无法忍受罗伊·摩尔。

sentences.en: So just so I understand, what percentage of white voters in Alabama voted for Jones in the end?
sentences.zh: 为了让我弄明白，阿拉巴马州最终有多少比例的白人选民投票给了琼斯？

sentences.en: Supported Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 支持了罗伊·摩尔。

sentences.en: But you have to keep in mind that at least 95 percent of African-Americans in the state supported Doug Jones.
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，该州至少95%的非裔美国人支持了道格·琼斯。

sentences.en: And the African-American vote comprised, according to the exit polls, 30 percent of the total electorate tonight.
sentences.zh: 根据出口民调，非裔美国人的选票占今晚总选民的30%。

sentences.en: That could be overstating it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 这可能有点夸大其词了。

sentences.en: But when you're winning that strongly among black voters and they're reaching towards 30 percent of the electorate, that really helps.
sentences.zh: 但当你能在黑人选民中取得如此强劲的优势，并且他们接近选民总数的30%时，这确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: And what about this write in strategy that we had talked to you about over the weekend?
sentences.zh: 那么我们周末跟你讨论过的这种另写候选人姓名的策略呢？

sentences.en: There was this sort of extraordinary thing where Senator Richard Shelby, who, as you explained, was once a Democrat, but is now very much a Republican,
sentences.zh: 当时有这样一件非同寻常的事，理查德·谢尔比参议员，正如你所解释的，他曾是一名民主党人，但现在是不折不扣的共和党人，

sentences.en: went on national TV and told voters to write in a Republican other than Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 他在全国电视节目中告诉选民，要在选票上手写填入罗伊·摩尔之外的一位共和党人。

sentences.en: I couldn't vote for Roy Moore.
sentences.zh: 我无法投票给罗伊·摩尔。

sentences.en: I didn't vote for Roy Moore, but I wrote in a distinguished
sentences.zh: 我没有投票给罗伊·摩尔，但我手写填入了一位杰出的

sentences.en: Republican name.
sentences.zh: 共和党人的名字。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people could do that.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Will they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们会这样做吗？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: And you were saying that a difference of a couple percentage points, if two percent or so of voters did that, could be meaningful.
sentences.zh: 你之前说过几个百分点的差异，如果百分之二左右的选民这样做了，可能会意义重大。

sentences.en: So did that happen?
sentences.zh: 所以这发生了吗？

sentences.en: That's exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 这正是发生的事情。

sentences.en: So in addition to a really strong turnout among upscale whites in the state of black population, the other real problem for Moore and effectively the backbreaker for Moore
sentences.zh: 因此，除了该州高档白人和黑人群体的高投票率之外，对摩尔而言另一个真正的问题、实际上也是击垮摩尔的致命一击是，

sentences.en: was the fact that 1.7 percent, so rounding up two percent of this state's voters, nearly 23,000 people
sentences.zh: 1.7%（四舍五入为该州选民的2%），近23,000人

sentences.en: took the time to use a writing instrument on their ballot and add in the name of a third party.
sentences.zh: 花时间在选票上使用书写工具写下了第三党候选人的名字。

sentences.en: That's a really high number in a special election like this.
sentences.zh: 在这样一场特别选举中，这是一个非常高的数字。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if we look at the amount by which Jones won, it was around two percent.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看一下琼斯获胜的优势，大约是百分之二。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So basically, the margin of victory is about equal to the number of people who wrote in the third party's name.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，获胜优势与手写第三党候选人名字的人数大致相当。

sentences.en: So why was Moore the Republican nominee if he was so hard for so many people's stomach?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然摩尔让这么多人难以忍受，为什么他会成为共和党候选人呢？

sentences.en: The short version, Michael, is this.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，简而言之是这样的。

sentences.en: He defeated a Republican named Luther Strange, who was appointed to fill the seat that was vacated by Jeff Sessions, who, of course, is now the attorney general.
sentences.zh: 他击败了一名叫路德·斯特兰奇的共和党人，后者被任命填补杰夫·塞申斯空出的席位，当然，塞申斯现在是司法部长。

sentences.en: Luther Strange got his seat through murky circumstances.
sentences.zh: 路德·斯特兰奇是通过模糊不清的情况获得这个席位的。

sentences.en: You know, murky perhaps is the best possible phrase I could use to describe it, was offered the seat by the governor of the state who was embroiled in a sex scandal of his own.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“模糊不清”也许是我能用来形容它的最好的词了，这个席位是由一位自身陷入性丑闻的州长提供给他的。

sentences.en: And there was some suggestion of a quid pro quo between Strange, who was then the state attorney general, and the disgraced governor.
sentences.zh: 并且有人暗示，当时担任州检察长的斯特兰奇与这位声名狼藉的州长之间存在某种利益交换。

sentences.en: So what happened, Michael, was that a lot of Republicans in the state saw what they viewed as a corrupt bargain between the now former governor and the caretaker appointee in the
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，迈克尔，该州的许多共和党人看到了他们认为的现前州长与该席位

sentences.en: seat.
sentences.zh: 的临时任命者之间的一场腐败交易。

sentences.en: That really hurt Strange, the appointee.
sentences.zh: 这严重伤害了斯特兰奇，也就是那个被任命者。

sentences.en: In comes Roy Moore, who's got a really durable base of conservative support in this state, heavily evangelical.
sentences.zh: 接着罗伊·摩尔登场了，他在该州拥有非常稳固的保守派支持基础，主要是福音派。

sentences.en: And he was able to turn the circumstances of Strange's appointment and Strange's ties to the kind of Washington establishment against him.
sentences.zh: 他能够把斯特兰奇的任命背景以及斯特兰奇与华盛顿建制派的联系转变为对付斯特兰奇的武器。

sentences.en: Alabama has been at a crossroads.
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马州一直处于十字路口。

sentences.en: We have been at crossroads in the paSt. And unfortunately, we have usually taken the wrong fork.
sentences.zh: 我们在过去也处于十字路口。不幸的是，我们通常选错了岔路口。

sentences.en: Tonight, ladies and gentlemen, you took the right road.
sentences.zh: 今晚，女士们先生们，你们走对了路。

sentences.en: So I think because maybe the assumption was that Roy Moore was going to pull this off, a lot of us don't really know much about Doug Jones, who's now been elected to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，也许因为大家假设罗伊·摩尔会赢得这场选举，我们许多人对现在当选参议员的道格·琼斯其实并不太了解。

sentences.en: So who is this new Democratic senator from Alabama?

Thank you, Jonathan.

sentences.zh: 爱你们。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: — I am truly, truly overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: ——我真的、真的很感动。

sentences.en: But you know, folks, and you have all heard me say this at one point or another in this campaign, I have always believed that the people of Alabama had more in
sentences.zh: 但你们知道吗，各位，你们都在这次竞选的某个时刻听我这样说过，我始终坚信阿拉巴马州人民的

sentences.en: common than to divide us.
sentences.zh: 共同点远多于分歧。

sentences.en: We have shown not just around the state of Alabama, but we have shown the country the way that we can be unified.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅向阿拉巴马州全境，也向整个国家展示了我们可以走向团结的方式。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, shortly before Roy Moore came out on stage and refused to concede, President Trump tweeted about the results in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 在周二晚上，就在罗伊·摩尔登场拒绝认输前不久，特朗普总统在推特上谈到了阿拉巴马州的选举结果。

sentences.en: Congratulations to Doug Jones on a hard-fought victory.
sentences.zh: 祝贺道格·琼斯通过艰苦奋战赢得胜利。

sentences.en: The write-in votes played a very big factor.
sentences.zh: 写入式选票发挥了非常大的作用。

sentences.en: But a win is a win.
sentences.zh: 但赢了就是赢了。

sentences.en: The people of Alabama are great.
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马州的人民很伟大。

sentences.en: And the Republicans will have another shot at this seat in a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在很短的时间内就会再次获得争夺这个席位的机会。

sentences.en: It never ends.
sentences.zh: 这一切永无止境。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你就可以做到。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, President Trump dismissed the accounts of the women coming forward for a second time with allegations that he sexually harassed them.
sentences.zh: 周二，特朗普总统第二次驳斥了那些出面指控他性骚扰的女性的陈述。

sentences.en: And he attacked Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, who has called on him to resign over
sentences.zh: 并且他攻击了参议员基尔斯滕·吉利布兰德，后者曾因性骚扰指控要求他辞职

sentences.en: the women's claiMs. In a series of tweets, President Trump said the women had fabricated their accounts
sentences.zh: 女性们的指控。在一系列推文中，特朗普总统表示这些女性捏造了她们的说法

sentences.en: and called Gillibrand a lightweight and flunky who would, quote, come to my office begging for campaign contributions not so long ago and would do anything for them.
sentences.zh: 并称吉利布兰德是“无足轻重的小角色”和“走狗”，并引用原话称，她不久前还“来我的办公室乞求竞选捐款，为了钱什么都肯做”。

sentences.en: Were you offended by the apparent insinuations in the president's tweets this morning?
sentences.zh: 您对总统今天早晨推文中显而易见的暗示感到被冒犯了吗？

sentences.en: It was a sexist smear attempting to silence my voice.
sentences.zh: 这是一场企图让我噤声的性别歧视污蔑。

sentences.en: And I will not be silenced on this issue.
sentences.zh: 在这件事情上，我绝不会闭口不言。

sentences.en: Neither will the women who stood up to the president yesterday.
sentences.zh: 昨天挺身而出对抗总统的女性们也不会。

sentences.en: Democratic senators denounced the president's tweet with Elizabeth
sentences.zh: 民主党参议员们谴责了总统的推文，伊丽莎白·

sentences.en: Warren asking Trump in her own tweet, are you really trying to bully, intimidate and slut shame
sentences.zh: 沃伦在自己的推文中质问特朗普：“你难道真的在试图霸凌、恐吓并用荡妇羞辱来对待

sentences.en: Senator Gillibrand?
sentences.zh: 吉利布兰德参议员吗？”

sentences.en: Gillibrand owed an apology for the misunderstanding of the president's tweet this morning because many, including the senator, thinks that it's about sexual innuendos.
sentences.zh: 吉利布兰德应该为误解总统今早的推文而道歉，因为包括这位参议员在内的许多人认为那是关于性暗示的。

sentences.en: At the White House on Monday afternoon, Press Secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders was asked about the exchange.
sentences.zh: 周一下午在白宫，新闻秘书莎拉·赫卡比·桑德斯被问及了这场交锋。

sentences.en: I think only if your mind is in the gutter would you have read it that way.
sentences.zh: 我认为只有思想龌龊的人才会那样解读它。

sentences.en: And so no.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 今天的《每日新闻》就到这里。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbar.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴尔。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您准备好迎接节假日的款待。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种遮光才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝断片了才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
